Good job! Just a few things:

  • Transitions. Transitions don't fit with the 'aww' theme here. If they must be kept, speed them up a bit. It feels glowy — good for a robotic or scifi subverse, but not here.
  • Colors. As seen in the image here, there's sky blue, dark blue, light blue, black, red, red-orange, orange, and white. Try: sky blue + white for backgrounds, black for text, and a darker blue for hyperlinks. Red text/hyperlinks and black backgrounds take away from the theme.
  • Fonts. Good design has two fonts (at most three, but rarely) — one for headings and one for body text. There are three in play here: Verdana, Nunito, and Imprima. Imprima goes well as a heading (and buttons), so keep that. As for Verdana and Nunito — one of them needs to go. Make sure the choice of fonts are consistant everywhere throughout the subverse.
  • Backgrounds. For the most part, the backgrounds are good; white is always great for a background. But, for some reason, the sidebar — as well as some text boxes, buttons, and the submission form — are playing rebel here. They should be white, too.

Also, the submission info text is gray — did you forget about it?

Why the limit to owning only 10 subverses?

The limit is not related to technology or resources and can be changed at any time to a, perhaps, more reasonable number.

There were users who owned over 100 subverses without actually using them which seriously ruins the "game" for everyone, so I decided to go with a limit of 10. My logic behind this was that anyone owning more than 10 subs is surely going to have a hard time moderating them all and keeping them in a decent shape.

The limit is open for discussion. What do you guys think is a reasonable limit?

With 10, I can see an argument for 20 (also taking common alternatively spelled versions, plural, acronyms) as seems to be the case with /v/AskWhoaverse and /v/AskWhoa. I can understand leaving it at a reasonable number. How about 32, the double of 16 and compatible with any legacy 5-bit systems out there. ;)

Anyway, allowing users/bots to take a huge number with no activity seems like a good honeypot to identify problem users to ban.

I know this a year old but I propose the limit be dynamic. Instead of limiting the # of subs a person can moderate, base the limit on the sum of subscribers that person is moderating instead. That way a user could theoretically moderate many small/inactive verses.

An additional advantage is that it would then be possible to create a system that automatically puts mods up for audit when they gain too much power (based on changes to the # of subscribers they moderate)
10 is plenty. There is no reason to make it easier for a small handful of individuals to wield greater influence over this site. There aren't any good reasons for someone to moderate 80 subverses.
